lead.headline: JPMorgan deploys JPM Coin on Ethereum for institutional settlement
lead.tldr: Today's signals point to a bifurcation: legacy finance is building compliant rails on public chains while crypto-native firms retreat to treasury games and buybacks. The value is shifting to regulated infrastructure plays.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today we are watching institutional incumbents colonize public blockchain infrastructure while crypto-native treasuries optimize for balance-sheet optics rather than product velocity.

top_signals.title: JPMorgan takes JPM Coin to Ethereum for institutional clients: Report59m, JPMorgan takes JPM Coin to Ethereum for institutional clients: ReportJPMorgan is reportedly expanding its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum, allowing institutional clients to make payments and settle tokenized asset transactions.
top_signals.summary: JPMorgan is reportedly expanding its JPM Coin deposit token to the Ethereum blockchain. This move aims to enable institutional clients to facilitate payments and settle tokenized asset transactions more efficiently.
top_signals.why_it_matters: JPMorgan's Ethereum deployment validates public chains for institutional-grade settlement and creates competitive pressure for private-permissioned alternatives to justify their existence.

top_signals.title: BlackRock files for bitcoin ETF offering downside protection and upside exposure to IBIT
top_signals.summary: BlackRock has filed with the SEC for a new ETF called the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protect ETF. This product aims to provide investors with upside exposure to Bitcoin while offering downside protection.
top_signals.why_it_matters: BlackRock's structured product filing reveals institutional demand for Bitcoin exposure with guardrails, suggesting the next growth vector is risk-managed wrappers rather than raw spot access.

top_signals.title: Visa, Mesh partner to enable crypto spending at 175M merchant locations25m
top_signals.summary: Visa has partnered with Mesh to expand the ability for users to spend cryptocurrency at approximately 175 million merchant locations. This integration aims to bridge the gap between digital assets and traditional retail payments.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Visa's 175-million-merchant integration normalizes crypto as a payment rail but abstracts away the underlying asset, commoditizing the interface layer.

top_signals.title: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers
top_signals.summary: Mastercard has launched 'Stablecoin Security', a risk screening tool designed to help banks and payment providers detect fraud and sanctions risks in stablecoin transactions. The service is expected to be available globally by 2027.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Mastercard's 2027 timeline for stablecoin risk screening indicates compliance infrastructure will be a prerequisite for bank participation, not a differentiator.

top_signals.title: Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal 24m, Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal The transaction would give Metaplanet access to US capital markets, where it plans to use preferred stock offerings to finance additional Bitcoin purchases.
top_signals.summary: Metaplanet is acquiring a 93.7% stake in Super League through a transaction involving 2,100 BTC. This strategic move is intended to provide Metaplanet with access to US capital markets to further finance its Bitcoin accumulation strategy.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Metaplanet's acquisition structure—using Bitcoin as acquisition currency to access US capital markets—demonstrates how corporate treasuries are becoming financial engineering vehicles rather than operating companies.

deals.summary: Strive has expanded its Bitcoin treasury by purchasing 4,045 BTC for $335 million. This acquisition brings their total holdings to 36,818 BTC, cementing their position as the fourth-largest public corporate holder of Bitcoin.

Solana treasury firm SkyAI has liquidated its entire SOL holdings to secure $223.8 million in cash. The company intends to use these funds to launch a buyback of up to 95% of its outstanding shares and warrants.
Strategy has acquired an additional $22 million worth of Bitcoin, marking its sixth purchase since August. The company is also increasing its planned share buybacks alongside this asset accumulation.

Strive has increased its Bitcoin holdings by purchasing an additional 1,223 BTC for approximately $100 million. This acquisition brings the company's total holdings to 36,818 BTC, placing it among the top four public company holders of the asset.

on_the_radar.title: Mastercard unveils Stablecoin Security tool to screen payments for fraud and sanctions risks
on_the_radar.summary: Mastercard has launched a new security tool designed to screen stablecoin payments for fraud and sanctions risks. The service provides banks with a risk score prior to transaction completion to enhance compliance and security.

on_the_radar.title: Zoom adds ‘proof of human’ badges to show you’re not a deepfake
on_the_radar.summary: Zoom has integrated World ID's biometric 'proof of human' badges for its enterprise users to combat AI-driven deepfake fraud. This partnership allows users to verify their identity, providing a critical security layer for financial firms and corporate clients.

on_the_radar.title: Market participants weigh in on SEC’s proposed crypto regulations
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC is closing the public comment period for proposed cryptocurrency regulations this week. This move follows the agency's suggestion of a workaround due to congressional delays regarding the CLARITY market structure bill.

on_the_radar.title: Filecoin: Solstice and the Shift to a Demand-Driven Service Economy
on_the_radar.summary: Filecoin is implementing 'Solstice', a strategic shift in its incentive structure. The goal is to move from rewarding the mere creation of storage capacity to incentivizing the generation of actual paid customer demand.

on_the_radar.title: Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto license to support global expansion33m, Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto license to support global expansionThe UK-based fintech will use the authorization to offer crypto services in additional international markets, though it has not disclosed specific countries or launch dates.
on_the_radar.summary: Revolut has obtained a crypto license from Gibraltar to facilitate the expansion of its digital asset services globally. While the fintech giant has not specified the exact markets or timelines, the authorization marks a strategic step in its international growth.

on_the_radar.title: SkyAI sells off entire Solana treasury as it launches $201 million buyback
on_the_radar.summary: SkyAI has liquidated its entire Solana treasury to facilitate a $201 million buyback program. Despite the sell-off, the company intends to develop a financial platform integrating AI with Solana-based stablecoin payments.

on_the_radar.title: Bitmine adds 12,535 ETH as treasury reaches 6.04 million tokens
on_the_radar.summary: Bitmine has expanded its treasury by acquiring an additional 12,535 ETH. The company now holds a total of 6.04 million tokens, representing approximately 4.9% of the total circulating supply of ether.

on_the_radar.title: Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan
on_the_radar.summary: Nine public companies have formally objected to their shares being offered as tokenized stocks on a platform developed by OKX and ICE. This highlights the ongoing tension between traditional corporate governance and the push for blockchain-based asset tokenization.

worth_a_read.title: Filecoin: Solstice and the Shift to a Demand-Driven Service Economy
worth_a_read.note: Filecoin's demand-driven service economy pivot offers a test case for whether decentralized storage can escape token subsidy dependency and achieve unit economics comparable to centralized alternatives.

worth_a_read.title: Memes Meet Stocks: Inside StonkFun, Pump’s Response and Solana’s Reward Coins
worth_a_read.note: The StonkFun analysis maps how Solana's reward coin mechanics are being weaponized for equity-like speculation, with regulatory implications worth tracking for any project blending memes with investment contracts.

linkedin_post:
JPMorgan's JPM Coin is now running on Ethereum. Not a pilot. Not a testnet. Production infrastructure for institutional clients to settle tokenized assets.

This matters differently than the headlines capture. For five years, the default assumption was that banks would build walled gardens—private chains, closed networks, proprietary tokens. JPMorgan itself launched Onyx on an internal ledger. The migration to Ethereum's public chain, even if permissioned at the application layer, concedes something important: the network effects are on the open protocol, not the bank's server farm.

We underwrite infrastructure on where the transaction volume migrates. Today that migration is toward regulated interfaces on public rails. Visa's 175 million merchant integration, Mastercard's stablecoin screening tool for 2027—each is a bet that compliance and distribution win over ideological purity.

Meanwhile SkyAI liquidates its SOL to buy back 95% of its shares. Strategy keeps accumulating Bitcoin with share buybacks as accompaniment. These are balance-sheet trades, not product bets. The contrast is stark.

The repricing we are watching: infrastructure with regulatory clearance trades at a premium to protocols without distribution. The test is whether Ethereum's fee base grows from institutional settlement volume, or whether JPMorgan's deployment remains a siloed endpoint. We will know by Q2 next year.
